items.task: RESUMED: a first session of this item died at the usage limit on 2026-11-24; continue from what this worktree and branch hold (tracks/core/JOURNAL-step-limit.md if it exists), redo nothing finished. Source item for release v0.7: the step limit and the gauge speeds (tracks/core/interfaces/REQUESTS_WAVE3.md item W31 on core/nrpic; coord/DECISIONS/0027 item 2). Track A found by runs in which it could have failed that the Gamma-driver shift goes unstable at the grid scale once the step exceeds 0.685 of the cell (RK4 with Kreiss-Oliger dissipation 0.5; 0.65 on a 64-cell root mesh; 0.77 to 0.80 without dissipation), while <z4c> dt_lightspeed counts the speed of light only (z4c_newdt.cpp), and that the relaxed lapse is stiff where lapse_leak times the step is large (its request with run ids and the stability analysis: tracks/A-emd-pbh/outbox/20261121T231546Z__to-core__periodic-gamma-driver-step.md and package tracks/A-emd-pbh/periodic_diag on branch track/A-emd-pbh; its reproducing inputs diag_uniform there). Work: (1) derive the characteristic speeds of the gauge sector as the code evolves it (the Gamma-driver with its shift_Gamma and shift_eta, 1+log with the relaxation term) and the stability bound of the scheme for each (repeat A's von Neumann analysis with the code's stencils, RK4 and dissipation; say where you agree and where not); (2) implement the step limit that counts them (z4c_newdt.cpp), as an option, and decide by the evidence whether the old behaviour is a defect that should change by default (then it is a change without an option and the changelog says so) or stays the default for bit-identical old runs; a warning at start-up when the chosen cfl_number and gauge make the step exceed the bound, and when lapse_leak times the step is beyond its bound; (3) tests, predictions first (tracks/core/JOURNAL-step-limit.md): A's uniform-mesh reproducer at cfl_number 1.0 goes unstable without the new limit and stays smooth with it at the same cfl_number; A's refined periodic deck through the time of its failure; cost of the smaller step; byte regression against release core-v0.6 with the option absent; one card smoke run (at most half a card-hour); (4) interface text tracks/core/interfaces/step_limit.md; an outbox message to Track A with the executable and the option. SECOND ITEM, in the same session if the first is closed, otherwise leave it named in the journal: preempted runs (coord/DECISIONS/0032 item 2). Jobs of another user in a partition of higher priority cancel ours for hours; AthenaK writes no restart file when it receives the termination signal, so a preempted segment is lost back to its last restart file. (a) In AthenaK: on the termination signal, finish the current cycle, write every restart output once, and exit cleanly (look at how the wall-clock limit and the signal flags are handled now; Slurm sends SIGTERM and after its grace period SIGKILL: measure the grace period on this machine with scontrol show config and say whether a 256-cell restart file can be written inside it). Test, prediction first: a periodic run on processors killed with SIGTERM part-way resumes from the restart file written on the signal and matches the uninterrupted run byte for byte; the same for a run with particles. (b) scripts/submit_chain.sh: an attempt ended by a preemption does not count against MAX_SEGMENTS (the tracks' chains died of this); the stray resubmission after a chain's last segment is removed; test with the fake-kill test of the earlier chain work. Byte regression against release core-v0.6. Interface text; outbox messages to the tracks.
